Brain freeze has a real scientific name, and it's a mouthful 🍦

It's called sphenopalatine ganglioneuralgia. Your brain itself has no pain sensors: cold hits the roof of your mouth, blood vessels there quickly widen to warm things up, and nerves report it as pain in the front of your head. It usually lasts a few seconds, up to two minutes. If you get frequent headaches that last a while, see a doctor.

Your brain isn't freezing. It's just hearing the complaints.

Sources: Cleveland Clinic, Swinburne University, Virginia Tech.
